injuries.injury_description: Landale won't suit up Friday and this will be his fifth consecutive absence. His next chance to play will come against the Knicks on Sunday.

Newell suffered the toe injury in the Nov. 4 win over Washington and is now set to miss an extended period. With Mouhamed Gueye (foot) expected to miss at least three more weeks, Aaron Wiggins and Corey Kispert could see a slight bump in minutes moving forward.

The veteran combo guard has been diagnosed with a left calf strain, and he's in line to miss the next month or so. Once rookie first-rounder Kingston Flemings (back) is healthy, he'll have a long runway as Atlanta's top point guard. Aaron Wiggins remains worth holding in nearly all fantasy leagues as well.

The team stated in July that the big man would remain sidelined for the next 3-to-4 months after undergoing surgery to repair a fractured left foot, and he's continuing to make progress in his rehab. A timetable for Gueye's 2026-27 debut has yet to be established, thought a date could come into focus following his next evaluation in mid-December.

Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

Neemias Queta should continue handling the bulk of Boston's center minutes, with Luka Garza and Chris Cenac potentially receiving additional opportunities. Robinson's next chance to return comes Sunday against the Spurs.
Wagner suffered an injury Wednesday against the Bucks and won't be an option Friday. His status for the second leg of the back-to-back set Saturday at Charlotte is uncertain.

Traore had a productive start to his second year in the NBA, though he's now set to miss an extended period after sustaining a hamstring injury in Friday's loss to Orlando. With the 20-year-old point guard sidelined, Egor Demin, Mikel Brown and Keon Ellis are candidates for increased playing time.

Kalkbrenner exited Monday's loss to Memphis early with left hip soreness and is now set to miss Wednesday's contest. His next chance to play will come Saturday against the Nets. With the big man sidelined, Hannes Steinbach could see meaningful playing time behind Moussa Diabate.

Allen will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to a concussion. With the veteran swingman sidelined, Sion James (thigh), Grant Williams and Royce O'Neale are candidates for increased playing time. Allen's next chance to play will come Saturday against Brooklyn.

Schroder remains out indefinitely with a hamstring strain. With Charlotte already eliminated from knockout-round contention in the NBA Cup, it's possible the veteran's point guard's absence extends into mid-December.

Knueppel missed the first eight games of the 2026-27 campaign. He returned for the 114-104 loss to Brooklyn on Wednesday, though he exited the contest after just six minutes of work and didn't return. With Knueppel out of commission for at least a month, Grayson Allen and Sion James are candidates to replace him in the starting lineup, especially with Dennis Schroder (hamstring) sidelined for a minimum of two weeks.

Smith is dealing with a gastrointestinal illness, so he won't suit up Wednesday versus the Hornets. Without him, Nic Claxton will presumably enter the starting lineup. Zach Collins might also be more involved.

Powell sustained the hamstring injury in Friday's loss to the Wizards and is now set to miss at least the next two contests. With the veteran swingman on the shelf, Isaac Okoro, Buddy Hield, Tre Jones and Patrick Williams are all candidates for increased playing time.

The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.

Tomlin, who is recovering from a lower back stress reaction, has yet to suit up for the Cavs this season. He continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff, indicating he's still not close, so he can be viewed as week-to-week moving forward.

Mobley is set to miss his third straight game Monday since suffering the injury, and he's slated to miss at least the next week while on the mend. The Cavs should have a better idea on when he'll return to the court as he begins to progress through the treatment and rehab phase.
Lawal will miss a fifth straight game due to a right groin strain. His next opportunity to suit up comes Monday against the Celtics.
De Larrea continues to miss time with a right knee strain, and it's not clear at this time where he's at in his rehab. He can be considered week-to-week until further notice.

Lively has yet to suit up this season after undergoing right foot surgery last December. Recent comments from head coach Dusty May indicate he is progressing in his recovery, but he will remain sidelined Friday.

Biberovic has yet to debut for the Mavs this season due to a right heel bursitis issue, and he doesn't have a clear return date. He should be considered week-to-week until the Mavs offer an update about his recovery.

Robinson is carrying a day-to-day tag due to a left quadriceps strain, but the veteran sharpshooter is not ready to play yet and will miss a sixth consecutive game Friday. This means Kevin Huerter will likely continue seeing increased playing time for as long as Robinson is sidelined.

Cunningham won't suit up Friday and will miss a second straight game, and the third of his last five, while dealing with right knee tendinopathy. This means Daniss Jenkins should run the point for Detroit on Friday, while Isaiah Joe could be in line for another start at shooting guard. Cunningham's next chance to return will come Sunday against the Magic.

Duren has been dealing with a hamstring strain since October, and his return is not yet expected in immediate contests. The fact that he has practiced with the G League club is still a good sign as he makes progress in his recovery. Duren would be a reliable source of production once he's healthy, but until then, John Collins and Paul Reed may continue to absorb his responsibilities at center.

Okorie has been diagnosed with an oblique strain, which he sustained in a G League game. The rookie first-rounder has logged a grand total of 20 minutes across five brief appearances, so his absence doesn't have major fantasy ramifications.

Prince last appeared in a game for Detroit on Nov. 14 and is now set to miss an extended period as he recovers from knee surgery. However, the veteran forward's absence shouldn't significantly impact Detroit's rotation.

Curry has missed six consecutive games, including Wednesday's tilt versus Sacramento, due to an oblique abdominal tear he sustained against the Rockets on Nov. 11. The Warriors will provide further updates following the holiday. Golden State has gone 1-4 with Curry sidelined, so hopefully Friday will bear some positive news for the 38-year-old.

Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.
The veteran center is now likely to be available Friday after first being deemed questionable to play. Nance offers the Pacers frontcourt depth along with Jay Huff and Kobe Brown.
Haliburton's return to practice is encouraging, but Indiana continues exercising caution with his hamstring injury. He is still expected to have his return in mid-December.

Oubre has been performing at a high level of late, scoring at least 15 points in six straight contests, but he could be forced to miss time due to a right hand injury. If he is out, Quenton Jackson could see extra minutes.

McConnell has missed the Pacers' last two games due to left hamstring soreness, and the questionable tag suggests the veteran floor general could be an option Friday. He's not expected to have a big role in most fantasy lineups, though, as he's averaging just 7.0 points, 4.3 assists, and 2.3 rebounds per game in his seven outings off the bench this season.

Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

Reaves practiced Wednesday, so he's trending in the right direction to face the Spurs, and a decision on his availability will likely come closer to Friday's 9:30 p.m. ET tipoff. Reaves has missed the last five games with a left heel contusion, so the Lakers have relied more on Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton and Jake LaRavia for backcourt contributions alongside Luka Doncic.

Stewart could miss Friday's game, and if so, it'd be a huge blow for the Grizzlies since Zach Edey (ankle) is also questionable. If both players are out, Taylor Hendricks would be the next in line to see heavy minutes at center. Stewart is averaging 10.6 points, 3.3 rebounds and 0.9 assists per game this season.

Edey didn't return to Wednesday's 115-97 win over the Clippers, finishing with seven points (3-4 FG, 1-1 FT), four rebounds, two assists and two blocks across nine minutes. Taylor Hendricks could be in line for a bigger role in the frontcourt Friday, as Isaiah Stewart (hip) is questionable as well.

Pippen hasn't been available for Memphis since Oct. 29 due to a lumbar disc herniation and remains without a clear timeline to return. He can be deemed week-to-week going forward, though his absence could extend into mid-December if the Grizzlies don't advance in the NBA Cup.

The rookie standout has been diagnosed with a moderate-grade ankle sprain, and he'll be sidelined for at least the next month or so. It's a tough blow for an upstart Grizzlies team, which will now rely even more heavily on Ty Jerome's playmaking for the foreseeable future. Taylor Hendricks has a chance to nail down a consistent role off the bench as well.

Grant suffered the injury during Thursday's 126-98 victory over Golden State. He will now be sidelined for at least two weeks, with the team expected to provide an update on his condition at that time. While Grant is on the shelf, Taylor Hendricks and Kris Murray are candidates for more minutes.

Jackson suffered a foot injury in Saturday's 129-110 win over the Nets. Head coach Tuomas Iisalo indicated after the game that the injury was "relatively serious," though it is now confirmed he will miss extended time. While Jackson is out of commission, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant should receive more playing time.

Saunders is still on the mend from a torn right ACL that he suffered during his final year at BYU. However, he has been cleared for on-court activities and will be allowed to practice with the Grizzlies now that he's officially signed with the team.

The fact that Antetokounmpo is probable suggests the star forward should have a decent chance to suit up Friday. He's been playing at a high level lately, recording four consecutive double-doubles and averaging 28.6 points, 12.9 rebounds, 5.3 assists and 1.6 blocks per game since the beginning of November.

Jakucionis will miss his second game of the season due to left ankle tenosynovitis. In his absence, Ryan Rollins, Caris LeVert and AJ Green could see expanded roles, while rookie Brayden Burries should also get a slight bump in minutes.

Ball exited Wednesday's game against the Thunder with a left ankle injury, and while he's carrying a questionable tag for Friday's game, his absence from shootaround casts doubt on his availability to face Memphis. A decision on Ball's status should be made closer to the 8:30 p.m. ET tipoff, but Ball's absence from shootaround is far from ideal. If he's out, Bones Hyland and Terrence Shannon would be in line to see more playing time in the backcourt alongside Ayo Dosunmu.

DiVincenzo suffered a ruptured right Achilles in late April but is seemingly ahead of schedule in his recovery. With the veteran guard and Anthony Edwards (knee) both sidelined, Bones Hyland and Terrence Shannon figure to continue seeing increased playing time.

Clark suffered a right hamstring strain during Saturday's 117-106 loss to Chicago. He played three minutes as a result of the injury, and he's now slated to miss at least two weeks and will be re-evaluated at that time. Terrence Shannon Jr. and Bones Hyland will see increased playing time off the bench in Clark's absence.

Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

Watford could be on the verge of making his return to the hardwood Friday after missing each of New Orleans' last nine games. However, he should be a depth option in the frontcourt and not much else when given the green light to return.

Mathurin has been dealing with plantar fasciitis for quite some time and hasn't suited up in any of the Pelicans' last six games. The doubtful tag leaves the door open for a potential return, but it wouldn't be surprising if he remains sidelined. Mathurin is averaging just 5.5 points, 1.8 rebounds and 1.2 assists per game this season.

Reese dropped a 15-point, 15-rebound double-double in the Squadron's win over the Mexico City Capitanes on Saturday and will return to the parent club ahead of its game Monday. Through five regular-season appearances at the NBA level this season, the big man is averaging 1.2 points and 1.0 rebounds in 5.4 minutes per tilt.

This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.
Friday marks a third straight absence for McBride. With the Knicks' backcourt a bit dinged up, Jose Alvarado could see enough playing time to warrant streaming attention in deeper fantasy setups.

Landry Shamet could remain in the starting lineup, while Josh Hart may absorb additional responsibilities on the wing. Anunoby's return to on-court activities is encouraging, but his next opportunity to play comes Sunday against Atlanta.
Plantar fasciitis is costing Clarkson a fifth consecutive contest Friday. His next chance to suit up arrives Sunday against the Hawks.

Towns is a new addition to the injury report, and the Knicks will reassess the star big man before Friday's 7 p.m. ET tipoff. Losing Towns would be a big blow for the Knicks since Andre Drummond (concussion) has already been ruled out.

Drummond played just nine minutes prior to exiting Wednesday's 121-102 win over Cleveland due to a concussion. Mohamed Diawara and James Wiseman will likely get a boost in playing time off the Knicks' bench with Drummond sidelined. His next chance to suit up will come against the Hawks on Sunday.

Topic has appeared in only three games for the Thunder this season. He's missed the last three contests because of a hip strain, with his next opportunity to suit up coming Saturday in Milwaukee. Without Topic, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix could continue to receive more playing time.

Williams has only played twice in the Thunder's last 11 games. It's unclear when he will be available to return, though his next opportunity to suit up will come Saturday in Milwaukee. With Aday Mara (shin) also ruled out, Kenrich Williams and Micah Peavy should both see more action versus the Timberwolves.

This will be Mara's third straight game on the inactive list, and for now, he should be considered questionable at best for Saturday's game in Milwaukee. With Jaylin Williams (back) also unavailable, Micah Peavy and Kenrich Williams will help back up Isaiah Hartenstein at the center position.

Williams remains sidelined following left ankle surgery, with no confirmed return date. His continued absence leaves Oklahoma City without a key offensive contributor, allowing additional opportunities for the Thunder's remaining perimeter players.

Once Sorber begins on-court work, there will be a ramp-up period before he's cleared for game-time action, so his absence will likely extend well beyond this initial 6-8-week window. Sorber was selected by the Thunder with the No. 15 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, but he missed his entire rookie season after tearing the ACL in his right knee and has yet to play this season due to right knee issues.

Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

Castleton squeezed five points and four boards into his brief appearance, including a successful three-point attempt. The reserve center made productive use of his late-game opportunity, though his limited playing time leaves his regular-season role uncertain.

Isaac continues to deal with a knee injury that has kept him out of action for the entire 2026-27 season. He should continue to be considered week to week until the Magic offer an update on his recovery process.

Nelson underwent surgery this offseason to repair a fractured left ankle. It's encouraging to hear that he's made some progress, but the two-way player can still be considered week-to-week moving forward.

Penda suffered a partially torn hamstring in the preseason and can still be considered week-to-week moving forward. With the second-year forward and Paolo Banchero (ankle) both sidelined, Tristan da Silva and Jamal Cain should continue seeing increased minutes.

Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

Embiid has missed Philadelphia's last two games due to an illness, but his presence at shootaround in Indianapolis is a good sign of a potential return to the court. The 76ers will provide another update on his status as tipoff approaches.

Brown is set to undergo imaging of his hamstring, but all signs point to the star forward being on the verge of another spell on the sidelines. Brown has been out for just three games this season, but if he's forced to miss more time, Dean Wade could see an uptick in his playing time.

Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.
Youngblood is in line for a ninth straight absence due to a bone bruise in his right foot. His next opportunity to run the floor will arrive Sunday against the Pelicans.

Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

LaVine will miss his second game of the 2026-27 campaign. His next opportunity to play will come Sunday against the Timberwolves. In the meantime, Leaky Black, Emanuel Sharp and Malik Monk are candidates for more minutes, with one of those players expected to move into the starting lineup.

Raynaud presumably joined the G League Kings for practice Wednesday. He's recovering from a right patellar subluxation and remains without a timetable to return, and while it's encouraging that he's getting reps with Stockton, the big man can be considered week-to-week until the Kings offer another update on his status.

Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

Harper has been upgraded to questionable ahead of Friday's contest despite reports on Nov. 19 suggesting he was set to miss two to three weeks due to a left hip external rotator strain. Julian Champagnie and Keldon Johnson are expected to retain expanded roles if Harper is ruled out.
Fox could miss a third straight game due to a right shin contusion. If he is unavailable, Jordan McLaughlin is expected to retain an expanded role.

Chris Haynes of NBA TV reported Friday that Harris is expected to ramp up his activity this week, and that the veteran forward could make his season debut as soon as early December. Until Harris is finally cleared to return from a calf strain, Julian Champagnie should continue to handle an expanded role on the wing.

The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

A decision on Martin's availability will be made closer to Friday's 7:30 p.m. tip-off, but his status shouldn't cause a big impact in most fantasy formats. He's averaging just 0.8 points and 2.2 rebounds on 12.2 minutes per game off the bench over his last five appearances.

Leonard continues to progress in his recovery, and the Raptors are expected to provide another update in a week. Collin Murray-Boyles and Allen Graves will likely continue seeing increased burn for as long as Leonard is sidelined.
Bittle continues to work his way back from a fractured right foot, as he's yet to make his 2026-27 season debut. He remains week-to-week until Toronto provides a definitive update.

Based on his re-evaluation timeline, Barrett likely won't return to game action until mid-December at the earliest. Jamison Battle, Allen Graves and Jamal Shead are candidates for increased playing time in Barrett's absence, especially while Kawhi Leonard (knee) is also sidelined.

Bamba's availability adds uncertainty to Utah's frontcourt rotation, with Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaxson Hayes (knee) also questionable. If Bamba sits, the Jazz could face a shortage of healthy centers against Denver.
Hayes could miss a second straight game due to a left knee strain. If he is unavailable, Mo Bamba figures to see an expanded role.

Nurkic could make his season debut Friday after being sidelined due to a partial plantar plate tear of the second toe on his right foot. If he is unavailable, Mo Bamba could see a large role, especially if Jaxson Hayes (knee, questionable) is also out.

Markkanen has missed two straight games due to what was being described as a right wrist sprain, but it appears the issue was much worse than initially thought. The talented big man now joins Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson (knee) on Utah's long-term injury list, while Keyonte George's status moving forward is unclear while dealing with an ankle sprain. Given all of the injuries, Ace Bailey and Darryn Peterson will have to lead the offense, while Isaiah Collier, Brice Sensabaugh, Svi Mykhailiuk, Josh Okogie and Josh Green are candidates for increased roles.

Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.
Vukcevic has yet to suit up this season due to a left hip injury. He can be considered week-to-week until the Wizards provide an update on his progress.

Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

Watkins, a two-way player for the Wizards, suffered the injury during the Summer League. Although Washington has yet to offer a timetable for a return, a typical recovery time for the procedure is approximately 9-to-12 months. That leaves Watkins in serious jeopardy of missing most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season, and it remains to be seen if the team will continue keeping him around on a two-way roster spot while he's injured.
